To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most common genetic alterations in thyroid nodules are in BRAF and RAS genes, and that the most commonly altered benign thyroid nodules were follicular adenomas.
genetic alterations in thyroid FNAS have a high specificity, but only moderate sensitivity, for predicting thyroid cancer.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the clinical application of RNA sequencing and the detection of genetic alterations in the diagnosis of thyroid cancer.
the application of next-generation sequencing to the detection of genetic alterations in thyroid neoplasms.
the diagnostic use of genetic alterations in thyroid neoplasms and the potential impact on patient care.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic alterations in thyroid neoplasms are a useful adjunct to the GEC in the preoperative evaluation of thyroid FNAs.
the genetic alteration panel alone is insufficient for the diagnosis of malignancy in FNAs, while a GEC may help to reduce the number of false positives.
a genetic alteration in a thyroid nodule is a marker for malignancy, but not sufficient for a diagnosis of malignancy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sensitivity of a panel of mutations for thyroid carcinoma in FNAs is 43 % and the specificity is 84 %.
the GEC is a more sensitive tool to detect thyroid cancer in FNA than the genetic alterations alone.
genetic alterations are not a reliable stand-alone predictor for malignancy in thyroid nodules, and that the use of genetic alterations in combination with a GEC may be more useful in this context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single mutation as a diagnostic test in thyroid FNAs is not ready for prime time.
genetic alterations are not specific for malignancy in thyroid nodules, but rather are a marker of neoplasm.
the genetic alterations detected by RNA sequencing do not appear to be sufficient to rule out thyroid cancer.
